diagnoses.analysis: This is the aggregate required-status check, not an independent build failure. The frozen reusable-pr-build.yml requires needs.test-latest-deps.result to be success and otherwise executes exit 1. Both failed latest-dependency jobs are caused by the scalar context propagation gap fixed in this candidate. No workflow change or rerun recommendation is needed.

The PR's independent-publisher regression fails because scalar sources are excluded from the propagation hook. The first mapper following Mono.just executes before the downstream TracingSubscriber activates the explicitly stored inner context, so it observes the outer application context instead. Removing the scalar exclusion lets the existing subscriber activate explicit root and non-root contexts before scalar callbacks. The complete latest-dependency Reactor library suite now passes, including all four cases of this regression; the Java 8 baseline suite also passes.

The installed-agent regression exposes the same scalar exclusion: an independent Mono.just mapper sees subscription context instead of explicitly stored root. The agent embeds the shared Reactor library, so the single shared-library fix also repairs this failure without changing agent advice or boundary ownership. The complete latest-dependency installed-agent, version34Test and initialization suites pass, as do their Java 8 baseline counterparts.

report.scope: Structural/Git verification only. No target code or tests are executed.

<!--
CHANGELOG.md is generated from merged pull requests. Do not add an entry unless this PR introduces
a deprecation or breaking change.
-->

Make explicit Reactor contexts authoritative, including root, and share operation/application boundaries between Spring AI and WebFlux clients. This changes the published alpha Reactor library contract for 3.0, not the core OpenTelemetry Context API.

Replace the stored-root workaround for transparent signals with `withoutSubscriptionContextCapture`:

```java
// Explicitly clear active context during signals:
ContextPropagationOperator.storeOpenTelemetryContext(reactorContext, Context.root());

// Preserve signal-time context without subscription-time capture:
ContextPropagationOperator.withoutSubscriptionContextCapture(reactorContext);
```

- **Context contract:** Preserve implicit-root transparency, spanless contexts, invalid spans, and retry behavior. Explicitly storing a context replaces the no-capture choice.
- **Shared boundary:** Add Mono/Flux `runWithContext(source, operationContext, applicationContext)` overloads. Scope upstream subscription, demand, and cancellation to the operation; calls to the immediate downstream subscriber to the application, including root. Downstream tracing subscribers retain their own context policy; the boundary does not carry an inner application context with values across merges. Asynchronous upstream propagation still requires registered hooks.
- **Client integration:** Reuse the boundary in Spring AI and WebFlux without changing span lifecycle ownership. Defer WebFlux exchange construction into the client context.
- **Agent compatibility:** Bridge capture control and both boundary contexts through agent-owned state. Preserve Reactor 3.1/Java 8 compatibility, existing two-argument helpers, and annotation lifecycle semantics.
metadata.title: Make Reactor contexts authoritative and share client context boundaries
